source_text: Chromatin Studio connects a model builder, a spatial simulation, and measurements from the current run. Each chromatin bead is a stretch of DNA, and its size is a model setting. This walkthrough uses one size throughout: two hundred base pairs per bead, about one nucleosome and its linker. The example is Manuscript hypotheses at eighty kilobases: four hundred beads of two hundred base pairs each. The default model and the small presets all use this size. Only the twenty-megabase presets keep coarse ten-kilobase beads, each standing for many nucleosomes, and they are not shown here. The center shows the applied model. Builder changes belong to the draft until they are applied. Begin by checking the bead size, the run status, and the physical-clock label.
